title: How Much Fiber in Dark Chocolate? 3.1g per Ounce
description: Dark Chocolate: about 3.1 g of fiber per 1 oz (11% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in dark chocolate?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Chocolate, dark, 70-85% cacao solids

intro: Dark chocolate ranks #2 of 7 nuts, seeds, and treats on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in dark chocolate by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in dark chocolate?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists chocolate, dark, 70-85% cacao solids at 10.9 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 oz (70–85% cacao); 28.4 g) therefore has about 3.1 g of fiber and 170 calories. That is 11% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 12% of a 25 g day and 8% of a 38 g day.
High-cacao dark chocolate carries real fiber from the cocoa solids, about 3 g per ounce. It is still a calorie-dense treat, but it is one of the few sweets that contributes to a fiber total.

sections.heading: Cacao percentage matters
paragraphs: The figures here are for 70–85% cacao. Milk chocolate and lower-percentage bars have less cocoa solid and more sugar, so their fiber is much lower.
Unsweetened cocoa powder is even more concentrated: USDA lists about 2 g of fiber per tablespoon.

sections.heading: How dark chocolate compares with other nuts, seeds, and treats
paragraphs: Of the 7 nuts, seeds, and treats on this site, dark chocolate ranks #2 for fiber per typical serving and #3 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 1.8 g of fiber per 100 calories, in the middle of the range for the foods on this site.

Close neighbors by serving: [pistachios](/fiber-in-pistachios) at 2.9 g (1 oz (about 49 kernels)); [flaxseed](/fiber-in-flaxseed) at 2.8 g (1 tbsp, whole); [almonds](/fiber-in-almonds) at 3.5 g (1 oz (about 23 almonds)). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), dark chocolate is #45 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding dark chocolate to your day
paragraphs: A square or two of dark chocolate with berries or almonds makes a fiber-friendly dessert.

Example: 1 oz dark chocolate, 1/2 cup raspberries. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 7.1 g of fiber, with 3.1 g from the dark chocolate. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of dark chocolate?
faqs.a: 10.9 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Chocolate, dark, 70-85% cacao solids). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in dark chocolate (1 square (about 10 g))?
faqs.a: About 1.1 g, for 10 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Is dark chocolate a good source of fiber?
faqs.a: An ounce of 70–85% dark chocolate has about 3 g, roughly 11% of the Daily Value, with around 170 calories.
Much less. Most milk chocolate has a gram or less per ounce.
